title: Capital Divide schemas
description: Project version 0.10. Two entity schemas in one file: Fighter and Item. Reference as schemas.json#/definitions/fighter and #/definitions/item.

fighter.title: Fighter
fighter.description: A combatant on a Capital Divide roster. v0.5: nothing leaves a Divide (DIVIDE_POLICY.md 5) — 'evacuated' redefined as field recovery to your own camp, not extraction. v0.4 added 'captured' status (rare, a negotiation asset per COMBAT.md 5) and pointed injury ids at the COMBAT.md 7 tables. Combat is entirely ranged (DESIGN.md 2.3) so aim is the sole attack aptitude. Note race != origin: any race may be a nattie, merc, or prisoner. v0.5 (Step 8.5b): several scalars were declared `integer` and have been continuous for steps. Nothing had ever validated a live fighter against this file, so the drift was invisible — a schema nobody reads is a comment. `arx.cjs regress` now walks real corps and their rosters against these definitions.

id.description: Unique snake_case id with ftr_ prefix, e.g. 'ftr_sczaa_vex'.

callsign.description: Broadcast nickname. Optional; typically earned through fame events.

race.description: Race id; canon sheets and naming conventions in RACES.md. The ankoth are a banished, non-playable lore race (canon) and are excluded by design.

origin.description: Recruitment pool of origin. Immutable — a freed prisoner who re-signs keeps origin 'prisoner'; the arc is their story.

age.description: Interpreted per-race via races.json (Step 2). Experience grows the mind; age erodes the body late (DESIGN.md 10). Svalbard primes run long.

stats.description: Seven visible ability scores, 1-20 FM-style. Ratified.

aim.description: Ranged weapon proficiency — the game's sole attack aptitude; combat has no close-quarters layer.

presence.description: Charisma and crowd appeal. Secondary captain stat.

resolve.description: Morale stability under fire and after losses.

potential.description: HIDDEN growth ceiling. Never shown raw to the player; scouts estimate it.

experience.description: Feeds development (Step 8) and battle composure (COMBAT.md 4.1): experience_bonus = min(18, 5*divides + 1.0*battles + 2*dividends), added to the per-engagement composure seed. Dividends buy nerve without buying risk.

traits.description: Trait ids from traits.json (Step 2). Racial trait pools (Et-y-Bellum devotion, Gil psionics, Svalbard tradition, etc.) per RACES.md.

type.description: Injury id from the COMBAT.md 7 tables: inj_arm, inj_leg, inj_torso, inj_head, inj_internal, inj_burns, inj_chest, inj_spinal, inj_catastrophic; Thythyn wing table inj_wing_tear, inj_wing_strut, inj_wing_spar, inj_wing_loss.

untreated.description: Untreated injuries degrade one severity step every 3 days during the Divide (COMBAT.md 7.1).

loyalty.description: Attachment to the corp/manager. Feeds captain doctrine fidelity and poaching resistance. Racially textured (Kellis high, Olmac low, Gil motive-driven, Thythyn status-coupled) per RACES.md. Declared `integer` and produced as a float since it became continuous; caught at Step 8.5b, the first time anything walked a live fighter against this schema.

fame.description: Per-fighter crowd standing. Single scalar stub until Step 7. Declared `integer` and produced as a float since it became continuous; caught at Step 8.5b, the first time anything walked a live fighter against this schema.

signing_cost.description: Merc signing bonus, prisoner auction price, or 0 for natties.

death_benefit.description: Paid on death. Highest for natties (family pensions on your own ship).

freedom.description: Prisoners only. divides_required is set PER CONTRACT (canon). On completion: status becomes 'freed', the Kier Bastille releases the contract, and the fighter may be offered a standard contract to stay (returning to 'active' with origin unchanged).

bond_partner.description: mon_wa only (canon): fighter id of the telepathically bonded half. Mon- is the first half, -Wa the second; the pair shares ONE roster slot and is DISTANCE-TETHERED (cannot be split-tasked beyond miles; forced separation risks collapse). On partner death, roll bond-shock: death (common) / braindead-retired (uncommon) / traumatized survivor (rare: scar traits + rename — widowed Mon takes the Em- prefix; widowed Wa takes the -Em suffix, proposed).

evacs.description: Times this fighter was carried out of a firefight alive — a near-death counter, and broadcast colour. Not departures from the Divide (v0.5).

notable_events.description: Event ids shaping this fighter's public story; feeds broadcast color and grudges.

status.description: 'freed' = completed freedom clause, currently unsigned; re-signing returns them to 'active'. 'captured' (v0.4) = taken alive by another corp mid-Divide — rare, resolved through negotiation (COMBAT.md 5). 'evacuated' (redefined v0.5) = carried out of the field to your OWN camp, alive but out for the remainder of this Divide; there is no extraction from a Divide, so this is field recovery, not departure. 'injured' is the between-Divides roster state. `prisoner` and `freed` were used by the code from Step 2 and missing from this enum until Step 8.6b, when the Bastille intake put enough of them on a roster for the new corp-schema check to notice.
status.note: Step 6 audit: 'evacuated' and 'released' removed. Nothing leaves a Divide (DESIGN.md v0.8 ruling), so 'evacuated' was dead by canon and no code ever assigned it; 'released' was never assigned either — a captive handed back by ransom or by their captor's whim comes home as 'injured', which is the truthful state to be in.

loadout.description: What this fighter carries, set at the M11 lock (PROCUREMENT.md 3). Five slots and two mod slots on the primary. Empty slots are filled by free Aleas issue kit. `kit` is the resolved stat block the combat resolver reads; the ids beside it are the record of what was actually bought.

mods.description: Item ids, slot 'mod', family-compatible with the primary.

sidearm.description: Item id, slot 'sidearm'. Fires only when the primary is dry, venting or damaged.

kit.description: Derived, not authored: resolved weapon/armor/sidearm stats, plus value and bulk. Rebuilt by sim/items.js on equip.

item.title: Item
item.description: A piece of gear, kit, or supply in the Capital Divide catalog. v0.4 (Step 5): race_locked struck — kit is kit, and the racial texture lives in traits (PROCUREMENT.md P10). Adds slot, family, price_model and the energy resource fields. Combat is entirely ranged (DESIGN.md 2.3); blades exist only as fiction, never as catalog items.

id.description: Unique snake_case id with itm_ prefix.

category.description: All weapons are ranged. Mods fit a primary; consumables are single-use.

tier.description: Rough quality band for procurement UI and sponsor-drop limits.

bulk.description: Logistics weight. Squad carry capacity and sponsor drops are bulk-capped, per the Aleas' 'reasonable limit' rule.

effects.description: v0 loose modifier bag. Finalized alongside COMBAT.md (Step 3).

range.description: Weapons only: the band this weapon fights best in.

tags.description: Quirks, from the PROCUREMENT.md 4.2 vocabulary. Every tag here must exist in items.json's quirks block and be read by the resolver; arx.cjs regress guards both directions.

heat_cap.description: Energy weapons: heat at which the weapon vents.

charge.description: Energy weapons: shots held by the cell before a night's recharge.

legality.description: Restricted items need Aleas paperwork (bribable). Contraband enters via smuggling and risks scandal if caught on broadcast.

uses.description: Consumables only (medical, supply). Omit for durable gear.

slot.description: Which of the five loadout slots this occupies (PROCUREMENT.md 3).

family.description: Resource model. Ballistic spends ammunition; energy spends heat and charge. Mods may be family-locked.

price_model.description: 'formula' prices regenerate from constants.pricing and are guarded by arx.cjs regress. 'scarcity' is hand-priced exotica. 'issue' is free Aleas kit. 'none' is contraband with no acquisition path before Step 9.

exotic.description: Tier-5 restricted kit, mostly reached through caches (PROCUREMENT.md 11.1).

identity.description: One line of fiction. Flavour only; nothing reads it.

action.description: Consumables only: which exchange-loop action spends it (PROCUREMENT.md 10).

examples.name: Breachgun
examples.identity: Doesn't shoot around cover. Shoots the cover.

examples.name: Beam Lance
examples.identity: A line drawn through the argument.

corp.title: Corp
corp.description: A competing company across a career: its people, its rack, its books, its standing with the boards and crowds, and what it has done. v0.1 (Step 8.5b). Promised since Step 8 and never written, which left the object the ENTIRE season loop is built around as the only major structure in the project with nothing checking its shape. Fields prefixed `_` are per-season working state written and consumed inside one pass of the loop; they are deliberately NOT described here, because a schema that pins working state turns every refactor into a data migration. What is described is the part that PERSISTS across a season boundary — which is exactly the part a save file would have to carry, and exactly the part that must not drift.

id.description: Corp id, matching an entry in oa_profiles.json.

profile.description: The OA profile this corp was opened from. Read-only reference data; the corp does not own it and must not mutate it.

roster.description: Everyone under contract, alive or not. The dead and retired stay on the roster within a season and are filtered at each use — S2's muster floor counts the living only.

armoury.description: The rack: item id -> how many are owned. Persists across seasons; grows by purchase and by loot, shrinks by kit left on the ground. PROCUREMENT.md 12.

treasury.description: May go negative; a corp that cannot pay asks the board (S5).

grant.description: The board's flat stipend. REPUTATION.md 6.5: it covers wages, the entry fee and arming a full force, and nothing else — which is why it is also the neutral point of the funding spectrum. It does NOT move with results, by ruling.

ledger.description: Every posting, in order. The books are the audit trail.

memory.description: What each audience has not forgotten yet.

patience.description: The board's remaining tolerance. At zero the manager is dismissed (S5). This is the fail state, and it is the only one — a corp is never struck for poverty (S12).

holds.description: What the board is stockpiling and how short it is.

goal.description: This season's card. R25: three or four discrete demands PLUS two standing ones scored on a spectrum. The standing pair is always present.

priority.description: The one demand that counts double.

standing.description: Exactly two, always: thrift and care. Scored in [-1,+1] and contributing in BOTH directions — a board is annoyed by an expensive year, not merely un-delighted by one.

interest.description: How much this board wants THIS planet. Drives the thrift weight, and through it how many bodies a corp sends.

casualties.description: Who this corp has spent, as the crowds remember it.

doctrineId.description: Which doctrine in items.json arms this corp.

underwritten.description: The board covered a shortfall this corp could not. S5 — a broke corp always gets one more year, at a price in patience.

dismissed.description: Patience reached zero and the manager was sacked. Written as a COUNT by `season.js` and read as truthy; declared as either rather than pretending it is a flag, because the schema describes what the code does.

history.description: One record a season, appended at close. This is the career — what the viewers read and what a save file would carry.

dropped.description: How many were sent. Between DROP_MIN and DROP_MAX, and a real choice since Step 8.5b — a corp sizes its drop by answering its board's funding demand (S3).

kitValue.description: Catalog value fielded. Must not exceed the Aleas ceiling, which is a CORP ceiling and does not shrink with the force (PROCUREMENT.md 2.2).

gearKept.description: Kit that came home because its owner would never drop it, whoever held the ground.
